I've struggled with this a lot in my life. A realization I had in later part of this year which has worked for me is to try to do more than you did the day before, until you gain a sense of your physical and mental limitations. Some people can push through those limitations but I think it would be wise to do so in isolated experimentations of one thing or another and see what you can do personally. "Willpower begets more willpower."

I have a bit of experience with this (5 year shut-in who dragged himself out by force of will). You build discipline through three things: contemplating, self-centered goals, and forgiveness.

  1. First thing you do when you wake up, stop. Don't check your phone/PC, don't text your friends, don't do anything. Just be: think about yourself in the morning, about how you're going to be fine. Social media fucks with our mood in the morning, distracts us. I'm not saying be positive or any of that bullshit: the goal isn't to be bright and cheerful. The goal is to be focused, ready to tackle something, without starting your day feeling bad for your friends, or lazy because someone else is slacking off, etc.

  2. Self-centered and multi-part goals. People make mistakes when trying to voice their goals by not making them about what they can do. For example: "I want to get laid (without paying)." Great, what can you do about that? You could try and make a ton of money, but still be ignored. Or you could train and get a body of a Greek god and people still might not fuck you. Re-phrase it: "I want a body that makes women stare." Good, now break that down, it might become: "I will go to the gym every day", it might be "I'm going to join a yoga class", etc. Never make a goal that you can't break down into actions that you can accomplish in the present. Also, NEVER tell anyone else your goals. Bragging about it and getting validation is what causes people to stop trying.

  3. Forgiveness. Want to know the #1 killer of discipline? Not forgiving a bad day. Maybe you signed up for a hobby you hate, maybe you missed a day of practice, etc. The thing that kills discipline is to go "Welp, I screwed up this time, might as well screw around today and start again tomorrow." Next thing you know, you're fat, you've wasted a year, and you're thinking about your "New Year's resolution". If you screw up, try and do something. Maybe you hate your spin class that you spend $100 on, but you can still go to the gym. Maybe each session of something is suffering, but you'll make a new friend you can be miserable with. This is how you keep trying.

Divide tasks into smaller sub tasks, as short as a few minutes per sub task. It's tough to say no to a few minutes of work. Space the sub tasks apart with as much free time as you feel like. Hours at first, if necessary. You'll still be making progress, and that will feel good, so you will be motivated to gradually shorten these rest periods.
